land.text: the Crimean peninsula and the steppe 'between the Dnieper and the Donets'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Predecessor: Golden Horde; Principality of Theodoro'. Theodoro is not listed as a land predecessor because the page has the Ottomans, not the khanate, conquer it in 1475. Hacı I Giray page: 'In March 1441, Genoese sources name him as the new khan' (1441 'often taken as the official start'), while 'Vasary says that the traditionally accepted date is August 1449', the date the golden-horde dossier uses.

land.text: the whole peninsula, annexed as the Taurida Oblast

successors.note: Annexed 8 April 1783 (O.S.; 19 April N.S.); 'formally incorporated into the Empire as Taurida Oblast during 1784' (Annexation page).

capitals.name: Eski Qırım (Staryi Krym)
capitals.note: Hacı I Giray page: 'He moved his capital from Stary Krim to the rock-fort of Chufut-Kale'; the page does not date the first seat, which the infobox of the Crimean Khanate page lists as Eski Qırım. Coordinates are the town's, the researcher's; the gazetteer has no 'Staryi Krym'.

capitals.name: Qırq Yer (Chufut-Kale)
capitals.note: Crimean Khanate page: Hacı I Giray took the throne in 1449, 'after which he moved its capital to Qırq Yer' (infobox 'Orda-i muazzam Kirkyir'); the Hacı I Giray page calls it 'Kyrk-Er' and 'the rock-fort of Chufut-Kale'.

capitals.name: Bakhchisaray (Bağçasaray)
capitals.note: The page: Bahçeseray 'was founded in 1532 by Sahib I Giray'; the infobox lists Bağçasaray as capital. The page dates the founding, not the move, so 1532 is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: the peninsula and the Dnieper-Donets steppe, carried back to 1441 from Cliopatria's 1468 shape; the page gives no outline of its own for these years

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Crimean shape begins in 1450, but the infobox says 'Established: 1441, by Hacı I Giray' (Hacı I Giray page: 'In March 1441, Genoese sources name him as the new khan'; the traditional date is August 1449); no page outlines the khanate for 1441-1449, so the 1468 shape (see crimean-khanate_1450) is carried back. The infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1468 shape for 1450-1467: the peninsula and the steppe between the Dnieper and the Donets; Budjak and Yedisan were only 'nominally subject' Nogai groups

keyframe_review.note: 222,809 km2 (west to 29.2E, the Dniester) against 135,385 km2 from 1468 (west to the Dnieper mouth). The page puts the khanate's steppe 'between the Dnieper and the Donets' and lists Budjak (Danube to Dniester) and Yedisan (Dniester to Bug) only as Nogai groups 'nominally subject' to the khan, undated. So the west strip (Dniester to Dnieper, about 90,000 km2 by the gazetteer) is a nominal Nogai dependency, not khanate land, and the 1468 shape is used for 1450-1467. The page gives no area, so no ratio.
135,385 km2: the peninsula (south coast excepted) and the steppe between the Dnieper and the Donets, as the page describes it. The page gives no area to compare.

135,292 km2, the same shape. In 1475 'Ottoman forces, under the command of Gedik Ahmet Pasha, conquered the Greek Principality of Theodoro and the Genoese colonies' and Meñli I Giray, imprisoned for three years, accepted Ottoman suzerainty (the footnote gives vassal status 'from 1475 to 1774'). The south coast was never in Cliopatria's khanate shape (south edge 44.65N), so nothing is removed; the vassal tint belongs to the Ottoman dossier (vassal_start 1475, vassal_end 1774, counterpart crimean-khanate).
136,570 km2 for 1487-1501: a 1 % refinement of the 1475 outline (135,292 km2); the page records no territorial change in these years.
136,685 km2. 'in 1502, the Crimean Khanate subjugated what remained of the Great Horde' (Great Horde page); the page names no land that passed to Crimea, so the shape is unchanged.
136,932 km2, the same outline to 1551. The page: 'from 1524 on, Crimean khans were appointed by the Sultan'; no land change.

136,825 km2. The conquests of Kazan (1552) and Astrakhan (1556) did not touch the khanate's land: 'After the collapse of the Astrakhan Khanate in 1556, an important element of the Crimean Khanate were the Nogays'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1579 shape carried back to 1572: the peninsula and the steppe west of the Don Cossack frontier, without the raid corridor to the Oka

keyframe_review.note: 115,147 km2 with a spike north to 55.6N, the latitude of the Oka near Serpukhov, where the 1572 horde crossed ('On 26 July 1572 the huge horde of the khan ... crossed the Oka River'). That is a raid, not territory: the infobox reads 'Crimean Tatar invasion of Russia repulsed' and the page names no gain or loss. The shape for 1572-1578 is the 1579 shape (the 1572 outline without the spike). The east strip beyond 36.8E that Cliopatria also drops in 1572 is explained by the ledger (it stays with the Small Horde, the Kuban Nogais).

86,139 km2, north to 49.2N, east to 39.2E. 'Don Cossacks reached lower Don, Donets and Azov by the 1580s and thus became the north-eastern neighbours of the khanate': the shape's east edge at Azov agrees. The page gives no area.

59,257 km2: 28,325 km2 of the 1594 shape (the gazetteer difference of the two shapes; bbox 34.2-38.3E, 44.8-49.2N, the steppe north and east of the isthmus) are gone. The page says only that the khanate's territory 'shifted throughout its existence' because of Cossack incursions and dates nothing, so the 1595 step is Cliopatria's (ledger event at confidence 1). (unverified: page budget)
58,984 km2, the same peninsula-and-Perekop outline; in 1648 İslâm III Giray's help aided the Cossack rising of Khmelnytsky (page), with no land change.
59,122 km2, unchanged outline; the Zaporozhian Cossacks appear as neighbours from 1662 (seed neighbours list).
59,168 km2, unchanged outline.
58,893 km2, unchanged outline.
59,122 km2, unchanged outline.
59,168 km2 for 1687-1737; 'the Treaty of Karlowitz (1699) outlawed further raids' changed no frontier on the page.

121,200 km2: the 63,000 km2 east strip (Azov coast and Kuban, 36.8-41.5E) returns, much the same strip as the 51,000 km2 Cliopatria removed in 1572. The page on the 1735-1739 war has the Treaty of Niš leave 'The Azak Fortress was demolished and its lands were turned into neutral territory'; this is Cliopatria's hand-over of the Small Horde's Kuban strip (ledger event at confidence 1, counterpart nogai-horde); no page opened dates it. The Crimean Khanate page lists a Kuban holding (the Kaztsiv ulus), undated. (unverified: page budget)
121,365 km2, unchanged; the war of 1768-1774 has begun.

123,558 km2: the south coast (3,035 km2 by the gazetteer) joins. 'In November 1772, representatives of Russia and Khan Sahib concluded the Treaty of Karasu Bazaar', which proclaimed an independent state 'including the former Kaffa Eyalet'. The Eyalet of Kefe page dates the eyalet's annexation to the khanate to the 1774 treaty instead; Cliopatria and the Annexation page say 1772.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1775 shape without Kerch and Yenikale, which Article XIX of the 1774 treaty left to Russia

keyframe_review.note: 123,400 km2. The treaty of 21 July 1774 left Kerch and Yenikale to Russia under 'full, perpetual, and incontestable' dominion (Article XIX); Cliopatria's 1775 shape still contains the Kerch peninsula, so a 25 km disc round Kerch is removed. The treaty also gave Kinburn to Russia (Article XVIII), which lies west of the shape's edge.
123,400 km2 for 1781-1782, unchanged; the Taman revolt of 1781-1782 and the restoration of the khan in October 1782 moved no frontier.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1782 shape, held to the annexation of April 1783

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends the khanate in 1782, but Catherine 'issued a formal proclamation of annexation on 19 April [O.S. 8 April] 1783'; the 1782 shape is carried through 1783.

region.text: the peninsula and the Dnieper-Donets steppe

ledger.note: March 1441: Hacı I Giray is named khan of Crimea. 'In March 1441, Genoese sources name him as the new khan' (the page takes 1441 as 'often' the official start; 'Vasary says that the traditionally accepted date is August 1449', the date in the golden-horde dossier); the Crimean Khanate infobox reads 'Established: 1441, by Hacı I Giray' and he 'warred for independence against the Horde from 1420 to 1441'. Neither page outlines the 1441 territory; the peninsula and the steppe between the Dnieper and the Donets stand for it.

1449: Hacı I Giray takes the throne and moves the capital to Qırq Yer. The page: he could 'ascend the throne of the khanate in 1449', 'after which he moved its capital to Qırq Yer (today part of Bahçeseray)'; the move itself is not dated, so 1449 is the accession year (confidence lowered from 3 by the ia-02-d reviewer).

1532: Bahçeseray, 'founded in 1532 by Sahib I Giray', becomes the khans' seat. The page dates the founding of the town; that it became the capital then is the researcher's reading (the infobox lists Bağçasaray as capital).

region.text: the Azov coast, Kerch, Taman and Kuban strip east of 36.8E that Cliopatria drops from the khanate in 1572 and gives the Small Horde

ledger.note: 1572: the Azov and Kuban strip stays with the Nogais. Cliopatria's Small Horde shape (the Lesser Nogai Horde, nogai-horde in this project) holds the strip alone from 1572 and shared it with the khanate in 1564-1571 (51,000 km2 overlap); the Nogai page: '1557 Mirza Kazy crosses the Volga and founds Small Horde along the Kuban', and this page calls the Black Sea Nogais 'nominally subject' to the khan. The Eyalet of Kefe page (formed 1568, direct Ottoman rule with sanjaks of Kerç, Taman and Azak) is the Ottoman reading of the same coast. The 1572 year and the counterpart are Cliopatria's: a bridging judgment.

region.text: the steppe between the Dnieper bend and the Azov coast (bbox 34.2-38.3E, 44.8-49.2N, 28,325 km2) that Cliopatria drops from the khanate in 1595

ledger.note: 1595: the northern steppe is lost. Page silent on the date: 'The territory controlled by the Crimean Khanate shifted throughout its existence' because of Cossack incursions; 'Don Cossacks reached lower Don, Donets and Azov by the 1580s'. The 1595 year and the 'nobody' counterpart (the Wild Fields, no state on Cliopatria's map) are bridging judgments.

region.text: Perekop and Bakhchisarai, the northern peninsula

ledger.note: May 1736: Russian troops storm Perekop. The page: they 'stormed the Crimean fortifications at Perekop and occupied Bakhchisarai on June 17'; 'The khan's palace was burned'. Half the army was then lost to fighting and disease.

region.text: Perekop, Bakhchisarai and Karasubazar, the northern peninsula

ledger.note: July 1737: the Russian invasions end. The page dates Lacy's march into Crimea and 'On 14 July, he burned Karasubazar' but not the withdrawal; the end of the contest is a bridging judgment (the later Treaty of Niš has Russia abandon its claims to Crimea).

region.text: the Azov coast, Kerch, Taman and Kuban strip (36.8-41.5E) that Cliopatria adds in 1738, the Small Horde's land to 1737

ledger.note: 1738: the Kuban strip passes to the khanate as Cliopatria's Small Horde row ends. 'The Nogays north of the Black Sea were nominally subject to the Crimean Khanate'; the Kuban holding of the Kaztsiv ulus and the Lesser Nogai Horde's 'Little Tartary' are undated on the page; the Russo-Turkish War page has Azak demolished and its lands neutral after the Treaty of Niš. The year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Russian army marched into Kaffa; the Russo-Turkish War of 1768-1774 'Russia invaded Crimea'

ledger.note: July 1771: the Russian army occupies Crimea. 'In July 1771, the Russian army marched into Kaffa, and the Ottoman governor of Kaffa Eyalet was forced to flee'. The page names Kaffa; the peninsula as the region is the researcher's reading. (Roles: Russia occupies khanate land.)

region.text: the peninsula, except the Kerch and Yeni-Kale garrisons

ledger.note: November 1772: the Russian occupation gives way to the treaty. Page silent on a withdrawal: 'Russian troops remained stationed in Crimea at Yeni-Kale and Kerch' after the treaty, and the 1774 treaty then left those two to Russia.

region.text: the south coast of Crimea, the former Kaffa Eyalet, added to the khanate in 1772

ledger.note: November 1772: the khanate takes the former Kaffa Eyalet. 'In November 1772, representatives of Russia and Khan Sahib concluded the Treaty of Karasu Bazaar'; the independent state proclaimed there included 'the former Kaffa Eyalet'. The Eyalet of Kefe page dates the same annexation to the 1774 treaty.

region.text: the fortresses of Kerch and Yenikale (Article XIX)

ledger.note: 21 July 1774: Kerch and Yenikale go to Russia. Article XIX: the fortresses 'shall remain under "full, perpetual, and incontestable" dominion of the Empire of Russia'. The same treaty made the Tatars of the Crimea 'politically independent' of the Ottomans.

region.text: Perekop, at the entrance to the peninsula

ledger.note: November 1776: Russian forces take Perekop. 'Catherine gave an order to invade Crimea in November 1776. Her forces quickly gained control of Perekop, at the entrance to the peninsula.' Şahin Giray, Russian-supported, crossed the Kerch Strait in January 1777 and was installed as a puppet khan. (Roles: Russia occupies khanate land; the Perekop isthmus is given by coordinate, no place name in the gazetteer.)

region.text: Perekop, at the entrance to the peninsula

ledger.note: April 1783: occupation becomes annexation. The page has no withdrawal date; the occupation of Perekop and the garrisons ends in the annexation proclaimed on 19 April [O.S. 8 April] 1783.

8 April 1783 (O.S.): Russia annexes the Crimean Khanate. 'The Russian Empire formally annexed the Crimean Khanate on 19 April [O.S. 8 April] 1783'; 'Crimea was formally incorporated into the Empire as "Taurida Oblast" during 1784'. The Crimean Khanate page: 'Catherine II intervened in the civil war, de facto annexing the whole peninsula as the Taurida Oblast'.

wars.name: Great Horde raids on Crimea under Sayid Ahmad (1445, 1452)
wars.outcome: 'In 1445, Sayid unsuccessfully besieged Perekop'; Sayid's 1452 raid 'ended with Sayid's defeat by Hacı'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The page dates Hacı's accession to March 1441 or August 1449; the Crimean Khanate page has him fight the Horde from 1420 to 1441.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Crimean coast (1475)

zones.text: the south and south-west coast and ports (Genoese Gothia, Theodoro), outside Cliopatria's khanate shape

wars.outcome: Ottoman forces under Gedik Ahmet Pasha conquered Theodoro and the Genoese colonies in 1475 (Mangup surrendered at the end of December 1475); Meñli I Giray was imprisoned three years for resisting and then accepted Ottoman suzerainty. The khanate lost no land of its own.
wars.note: The Principality of Theodoro page dates the siege from September and the surrender of Mangup to 'the end of December 1475', and has the Crimean khan allied with the sultan in a 20 June message.

wars.name: Crimean war on the Great Horde (1502)
wars.outcome: Meñli I Giray 'defeated the last khan of the Great Horde', ending its claims on Crimea; the page names no land that passed to the khanate.
wars.note: The Great Horde page: 'in 1502, the Crimean Khanate subjugated what remained of the Great Horde'; the golden-horde dossier carries the 10 June and 28 June dates.

wars.name: Crimean invasion of Russia and Battle of Molodi (1571-1572)
wars.outcome: Devlet I Giray sacked and burned Moscow in 1571; in 1572 the horde crossed the Oka on 26 July and was destroyed in the fighting of 29 July to 2 August. 'Russo-Cossack victory'; 'only 20,000 Tatar horsemen returned to the Crimea'. No territorial change on the page.
wars.note: The Crimean Khanate page adds that after Molodi the khanate 'lost access to the Volga once and for all'.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1735-1739), Crimean campaigns
wars.outcome: Russian armies stormed Perekop (May 1736), took Bakhchisarai on 17 June 1736 and burned Karasubazar on 14 July 1737, losing half their strength; the Treaty of Niš had Russia abandon its claims to Crimea, and Azak was demolished and its lands made neutral.
wars.note: The Crimean Khanate page: 'the Russians, under the command of Field-Marshal Münnich, penetrated the Crimean Peninsula itself'.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774) in Crimea
wars.outcome: Russia marched into Kaffa in July 1771; the Treaty of Karasu Bazaar (November 1772) proclaimed an independent khanate; the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (21 July 1774) made the Tatars 'politically independent' and left Kerch, Yenikale, Kinburn and Azov to Russia.
wars.note: Treaty terms from the Küçük Kaynarca page (Articles XVIII-XX).

wars.name: Russian annexation of Crimea (1776-1783)
wars.outcome: Russia invaded in November 1776, took Perekop and installed Şahin Giray (January 1777); Russian forces crushed a revolt at Yeni-Kale in February 1778; the Ottomans signed the Convention of Aynali Kavak in early 1779; a rebellion from 1781 ended with the khan restored in October 1782; Catherine proclaimed the annexation on 8 April (O.S.) 1783.
wars.note: The Treaty of Constantinople of 28 December 1783 [O.S. 8 January 1784] followed (Annexation page).

certainty.note: The steppe frontier with the Don Cossacks, the Zaporozhian host and the Nogai hordes is approximate throughout. Exceptions: the Kerch and Yenikale enclave given to Russia by treaty in 1774 and the Perekop isthmus line are sharp.

sources.title: Crimean Khanate
sources.note: Identity, 1441 founding, capitals, the Ottoman suzerainty (1475-1774), territory between the Dnieper and the Donets, Nogai groups, 1783; the page gives no area.

sources.title: Eyalet of Kefe
sources.note: Ottoman direct rule of the Kefe coast from 1568; sanjaks of Kerç, Taman and Azak; the page dates the eyalet's transfer to the khanate to 1774.

sources.title: Battle of Molodi
sources.note: 1571 and 1572 Crimean invasions of Russia; no territorial change.

sources.title: Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Empire
sources.note: 1771 invasion, 1772 Karasu Bazaar, 1776 Perekop, 1777-1783, annexation of 8 April (O.S.) 1783.

sources.title: Great Horde
sources.note: 1502 subjugation of the Great Horde's remnants by the Crimean Khanate.

sources.title: Russo-Turkish War (1735-1739)
sources.note: Crimean campaigns of 1736-1737; Treaty of Niš on Azak and Crimea.

sources.title: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
sources.note: 21 July 1774: independence of the Crimean Tatars, Kerch and Yenikale, Kinburn, Azov.

sources.title: Principality of Theodoro
sources.note: Siege and surrender of Mangup, September-December 1475; extent of Theodoro's coast.

sources.title: Nogai Horde
sources.note: Black Sea Nogais 'nominally subject' to the khanate; used for the Nogai Horde dossier as well.

sources.title: Hacı I Giray
sources.note: Opened after the other nine to settle the founding: March 1441 (Genoese sources) against the traditional August 1449; first capital Stary Krim, then Chufut-Kale; Sayid Ahmad's raids of 1445 and 1452.

notes:
Written for batch ia-02-d. Ten pages opened (budget 9 for 21 shapes, one over: the Hacı I Giray page was added last to settle the founding date; the Nogai Horde page is shared with nogai-horde).
Settled: capital moves 1449 (Qırq Yer) and 1532 (Bakhchisaray); the Ottoman suzerainty 1475-1774 (page footnote); the 1772 Karasu Bazaar gain of the south coast; the 1774 loss of Kerch and Yenikale; the annexation of 8 April (O.S.) 1783.
Corrected: crimean-khanate_1450 (west strip to the Dniester is a nominal Nogai dependency, not khanate land: 1468 shape used for 1450-1467), crimean-khanate_1572 (the raid corridor to the Oka is not territory: 1579 shape used for 1572-1578), crimean-khanate_1775 (Kerch and Yenikale removed). New keyframes: 1441 (infobox founding year) and 1783 (annexation).
Cliopatria steps that no page dates, kept as confidence-1 ledger events: the 1572 loss of the Azov-Kuban strip to the Small Horde row (the Kuban Nogais; that row is the nogai-horde dossier, whose shape holds the strip alone from 1572 and overlaps the khanate's in 1564-1571), the 1595 loss of the northern steppe (counterpart nobody) and the 1738 gain of the strip when the Small Horde row ends (the Eyalet of Kefe formed in 1568 with Kerç, Taman and Azak sanjaks is the Ottoman view of the same coast; the Niš treaty made Azak's lands neutral).
Disagreements: founding March 1441 (Hacı I Giray page, Crimean Khanate infobox) against the traditional August 1449 (same page; the golden-horde dossier) - both are on the page, 1441 is used; the transfer of the Kefe coast to the khanate 1772 (Annexation page, Cliopatria) against 1774 (Eyalet of Kefe page).
For other dossiers: the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should carry vassal_start 1475 and vassal_end 1774 with counterpart crimean-khanate, and the 1772 loss of the Kefe coast (counterpart crimean-khanate); russian-empire should carry the 1774 gain of Kerch and Yenikale, occupation events 1771-1772 and 1776-1783, and the 1783 gain; the Nogai groups north of the Black Sea (Budjak, Yedisan, Jamboyluk, Yedickul, Kuban) were 'nominally subject' to the khan, undated on the page, and are not drawn (a vassal-tint candidate once a page dates them).
Not opened (budget): Meñli I Giray, Russo-Crimean Wars, Treaty of Karlowitz, Pruth campaign of 1711 (not on the Crimean page), Zaporozhian Cossacks, Don Cossacks, Yedisan, Budjak, Little Tartary, Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774), Treaty of Constantinople 1783.
Gazetteer: no place 'Perekop' (a 40 km disc round 46.15N 33.70E is used); no region 'Yedisan'.
